# Shopware Storefront — SCSS variables, functions and mixins

Everything a theme can override without writing a single rule. Change a variable and it reaches every component that derives from it; write a rule and you have changed one place.

**977 Bootstrap variables, 179 Shopware variables, 400 CSS custom properties, 27 functions, 84 mixins, 26 theme configuration fields.**

## Contents

- [How to override a variable](#how-to-override-a-variable)
- [Theme configuration fields](#theme-configuration-fields)
- [Shopware variables](#shopware-variables)
- [Bootstrap variables](#bootstrap-variables)
- [CSS custom properties](#css-custom-properties)
- [Functions](#functions)
- [Mixins](#mixins)

## How to override a variable

A variable declared with `!default` takes your value if you set it **before** the file that declares it is imported. In a theme that means your own SCSS entry point, which the theme compiler loads ahead of the Storefront's:

```scss
// <your-theme>/src/Resources/app/storefront/src/scss/overrides.scss
$primary: #c81e1e;
$border-radius: 0;
$container-max-widths: (sm: 540px, md: 720px, lg: 960px, xl: 1320px);
```

Declare it in `theme.json` under `style`, before `@Storefront`. A variable **without** `!default` is not meant to be overridden this way — assign to it after the import, or change the rule that uses it.

Three reasons a variable override appears to do nothing: it was set after the declaring import; the value is also fixed by a `skin/` file later in the cascade; or the component reads a `--bs-*` custom property at runtime, which a compile-time variable no longer controls. In the last case set the custom property instead.

## Theme configuration fields

Declared in `theme.json`, editable in the administration, and injected as SCSS variables of the same name. Prefer these over hard-coded values for anything a shop owner might change.

| Field | Type | Default | Tab |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$sw-background-color` | color | `#fff` | themeColors |
| `$sw-border-color` | color | `#798490` | themeColors |
| `$sw-breakpoint-lg` | number | `992` | eCommerce |
| `$sw-breakpoint-md` | number | `768` | eCommerce |
| `$sw-breakpoint-sm` | number | `576` | eCommerce |
| `$sw-breakpoint-xl` | number | `1200` | eCommerce |
| `$sw-breakpoint-xs` | number | `0` | eCommerce |
| `$sw-breakpoint-xxl` | number | `1400` | eCommerce |

| `$sw-color-brand-secondary` | color | `#474a57` | themeColors |
| `$sw-color-buy-button` | color | `#0042a0` | eCommerce |
| `$sw-color-buy-button-text` | color | `#fff` | eCommerce |
| `$sw-color-danger` | color | `#c20017` | statusColors |
| `$sw-color-info` | color | `#005b99` | statusColors |

## Bootstrap variables

From the vendored Bootstrap. Grouped by the file that declares them, which is also how the upstream documentation is organised.

### _functions.scss

| Variable | Default | Overridable |
|---|---|---|
| `$_luminance-list` | `.0008 .001 .0011 .0013 .0015 .0017 .002 .0022 .0025 .0027 .003 .0033 .` | no |

| Variable | Default | Overridable |
|---|---|---|
| `$gutters` | `$spacers` | yes |

## CSS custom properties

Emitted at runtime, so they can be changed per element, per media query or from JavaScript — unlike an SCSS variable, which is fixed at compile time. `#{$prefix}` resolves to `bs-`, so `--#{$prefix}body-color` reaches the page as `--bs-body-color`.

## Mixins

Include with `@include <name>(<args>)`. `media-breakpoint-up` and `media-breakpoint-down` are the ones a theme uses most — they keep responsive rules on the same breakpoints as the grid.
